title: LESS-HSGUM-22405 - Getting ready to swim - Supplementary resources

textRun.content: This additional material is to be used to inform the activities in the ‘Rules circuit’.
Pupils move around the room while listening for the whistles.
walking in a stretched position with arms above the head
spring jumps; bending the knees and springing up high with the arms extended above the head
when a whistle is blown following the whistle code the pupils perform the correct actions:
1 short whistle blast: “get the attention of the swimmer”, pupils stop what they are doing and look at the swimming teacher
2 short blasts: “get the attention of another lifeguard”, pupils pretend to be a lifeguard looking at the pool holding a “torpedo buoy” and looking at the “pool”

3 short blasts: emergency, lifeguard requires immediate assistance, lifeguard taking action, pupils clear the “pool” immediately, quickly and safely by pretending to clear the “pool” and stand back away from the “pool” and wait for instructions
1 long blast: clear the pool safely and quickly
: pupils sit on a gymnastics bench, they put both hands to one side of the body and turn and lower themselves into the “water”

pupils perform an exit over the side of the gymnastics table by placing two hands on the table, pushing up with their hands, putting their knees onto the table and then lowering themselves safely onto the mat
Pupils sit on a bench with their hands at the side of their legs and kick in an alternating action. Keep the legs straight, toes pointed with knees and ankles relaxed.
. Produced in partnership with PE Scholar in collaboration with Swim England.
